1.why: Every MFA endpoint requires authenticatedSession(request, "authenticated"), which validates the session server-side against account.id and never trusts client-supplied user identifiers.

2.why: The identity code is stored as a hash bound to the issuing session, is single-use (identityCodeUsed) and expires in 5 minutes, so it cannot be replayed by any other session or user.

3.why: The /api/mfa/activate handler neither invalidates nor rotates the session, so sessions that existed before MFA enablement continue to work afterward.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-256-GCM-encrypted and backup codes as salted, peppered SHA-256 hashes, but the secret also exists as the hardcoded plaintext constant EVALUATION_TOTP_SECRET in the source.

5.why: Identity codes, backup codes, session IDs, CSRF tokens, and keys use crypto.randomBytes (CSPRNG), yet the OTP shared secret itself is a fixed hardcoded constant rather than randomly generated.

6.why: The only cookie (mfa_session) is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and the client uses no localStorage/sessionStorage, keeping the CSRF token only in an in-memory variable.

7.why: All inputs are validated server-side via validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, validRecovery, a regex on manualSecret, and strict JSON body shape checks.

8.why: Dynamic values (email, phone, secret, codes, messages) are rendered exclusively via textContent, the single innerHTML use is static markup, and a strict nonce-based CSP blocks inline script execution.

9.why: The signin handler rejects any redirect value other than the single internal path "/verify-identity" and the server never issues redirects to user-controlled destinations.

10.why: securityHeaders applies CSP (including frame-ancestors 'none'), HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY consistently to HTML, API, 404, OPTIONS, and error responses.

11.why: sessionCookie() emits the mfa_session cookie with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes (plus Max-Age).

12.why: Although server errors are generic and stack-trace-free, the client log() function writes the identity code, the TOTP seed, and all backup codes to console.log and an on-page "Logs" panel.

13.why: Identity codes are single-use with 5-minute expiry, TOTP codes are time-bound with replay blocked via lastAcceptedTotpCounter, and backup codes are marked used upon consumption.

14.why: failure() counts every failed or malformed attempt and locks both session and account for 10 minutes after 5 failures, with lockActive enforced on all verification endpoints.

15.why: On successful identity verification the old session is deleted and a fresh authenticated session ID issued, idle (15 min) and absolute (8 h) timeouts are enforced, and /api/logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
